column12: two caveats, both small. The 2024 CMS row combines two presentations, the 100 mg used in psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis and the 200 mg used in ulcerative colitis and Crohn's maintenance, which is dosed every 4 weeks; a beneficiary on the 4-weekly schedule consumes more doses a year than the 8-weekly denominator assumes, which biases measured retention up and this figure down. Gross cost per dose fell from $13,584 (2023) to $12,828 (2024), so the mix did not shift to a larger or more expensive presentation. And a year that contains a week-0 and week-4 loading dose holds 7 rather than 6.52 doses, which biases the same way. No published guselkumab persistence study is used, because the CMS series measures the same beneficiaries the price is quoted on

column11: already approved, so the reported revenue contains these patients. On 2025-09-29 the FDA approved TREMFYA for pediatric plaque psoriasis and active psoriatic arthritis, and the current label reads 'adults and pediatric patients 6 years of age and older who also weigh at least 40 kg with active psoriatic arthritis' (TREMFYA USPI, DailyMed setid 1e6dc9ae-1c4c-42d9-87aa-c315ecc51b56). The guselkumab programme in juvenile arthritis is juvenile psoriatic arthritis alone: PSUMMIT-Jr (NCT05083182, Phase 3, 48 participants, completed 2026-01-12) enrols 'juvenile psoriatic arthritis (jPsA) by Vancouver criteria with exclusion of enthesitis-related arthritis', and NCT06663332, the trial the book reads as the pending Phase 3, is an open-label basket long-term extension that admits only participants who have completed a primary paediatric guselkumab study. No pool is seeded, because a layer wholly inside the approved business adds nothing whatever its prevalence is
column12: the residual, stated rather than priced. The label excludes patients under 6 years and patients 6 or over who weigh under 40 kg, and PSUMMIT-Jr enrolled from age 5 with no weight floor in its stated criteria, so a band of younger and lighter children with juvenile psoriatic arthritis does sit outside the label and is a genuine incremental layer by the test the brief sets. It is left out because the share could not be sourced: CDC growth charts put the 50th percentile for weight at 40 kg at around age 12, which would make the band large, but no published weight or age distribution for juvenile psoriatic arthritis was found to multiply the book's 4,900-patient pool by, and guessing one would be the invented row this file exists to avoid. A paediatric weight or age distribution for jPsA, or PSUMMIT-Jr's own enrolled weight distribution when it publishes, would settle it
